title: Crocodiles Can't Chew, So They Spin Instead

scenes.text: Crocodiles can't chew, so they spin.
Their cone-shaped teeth can't cut or grind meat, so they use the death roll.
An alligator tucks in its legs and whips its tail sideways to start the spin.
Pulling in like a figure skater makes it spin faster. Young alligators in one study rolled about one and a half times a second.
Nobody teaches them. Alligators raised from eggs in a lab did it right away when given meat.

description:
Alligators and crocodiles can't chew, so they spin their whole body to tear off pieces of prey.
Scientists found that young alligators do it by instinct, and they spin faster by tucking in their limbs like a figure skater.
Have you seen one do it?
first_comment: Which predator is scarier to you, an alligator or a crocodile?
